# Firestore queries and indexes

## Change a serving query

Add or update a runtime query driver in `backend/tests/support/firestore_query_driver_registry.py`; use named caller witnesses when serving helpers are called from routes or services. Drivers execute the real builder against `RecordingFirestore` across its argument profiles. The guard requires every serving shape to be classified, certain, and served by the generated manifest. A failure reports the driver/profile, query shape, and candidate index. Fix the query shape or declare its required index in the same PR. Run `backend/tests/unit/test_firestore_query_shapes.py` and `backend/tests/unit/test_firestore_outside_query_contract.py`.

The backend unit selector includes the Firestore index guard set for every Python source file in the serving-query inventory, including router and helper changes, plus changes to `firestore.indexes.json`, the index registry, and Firestore guard support files. The canonical `firestore-index-guard` manifest check reuses that selector in both local preflight and Release Eligibility, runs only the seven guard files through `backend/test.sh` in a pinned Python environment, and blocks proof for a failing main SHA even if `Backend unit suite` was merged over. Environment/setup errors fail closed with a separate diagnostic; restore the guard environment and rerun rather than skipping it. `Backend unit suite` is not currently a required branch-protection check. The release check is diff-scoped: a later unrelated SHA can receive proof without rerunning it, and explicit `skip_eligibility_proof` break-glass remains an operator bypass.

`GET /v1/conversations` and `/v1/conversations/count` reject multiple sources combined with multiple statuses and cap each list at 20 (`MAX_IN_FILTER_VALUES`), so the Firestore disjunction limit is not reachable through these routes.

## Declare an index

Edit `backend/database/firestore_index_registry.py`, then run:

```bash
backend/.venv/bin/python backend/scripts/generate_firestore_indexes.py --write
```

Commit the registry and generated `firestore.indexes.json` together. Do not hand-edit the generated manifest or create undeclared indexes directly in a project. Single-field collection-group requirements are field requirements in the registry and generated `fieldOverrides`; an oracle `create_exemption=` suggestion belongs on this path, not in a composite query spec.

## Apply and deploy

Merging a manifest PR triggers `.github/workflows/gcp_firestore_indexes.yml`. Dev applies automatically; prod requires approval. Every backend-source image shipment — deploy, job, or Helm upgrade — passes the shared `.github/actions/firestore-readiness` composite first. Each caller stages the gate controls from its own immutable `github.workflow_sha` into .github/firestore-workflow after the runtime-source checkout, then the composite checks out the exact admitted `source_sha`, verifies its `firestore.indexes.json` was generated by that commit's registry (a pre-registry commit's checked-in manifest is validated structurally instead), and `--check-only`s `vars.RUNTIME_GCP_PROJECT_ID` on the `(default)` database with read-only `GCP_FIRESTORE_READONLY_CREDENTIALS` in an isolated `CLOUDSDK_CONFIG` so deploy credentials can never win. JIT QA lanes target `env.QA_PROJECT`/`env.QA_FIRESTORE_DATABASE`. `gcp_backend_listen_helm.yml` gates only its explicit-tag path: kept-tag and rollback lanes replay an image already served in the same environment and the index pipeline is create-only, so the shared gate is conditioned on `env.BACKEND_LISTEN_SOURCE_SHA != ''` and rollback gains no new failure mode. The sync-ledger cutover consumes an operator-supplied backend image (nominal contract: only images published by the gated builders `gcp_backend.yml`/`gcp_backend_auto_dev.yml`; the workflow's generic `@sha256` digest check does not enforce the repository) and never builds one, so it runs no gate of its own. A failed gate blocks the shipment and uploads a locally revalidated, short-TTL proposal artifact for the apply lane. Schedule the production approval and index build before a backend release that depends on the new index. Reconciliation creates missing composites and union-preserving field indexes; destructive `indexes=[]` exemptions use the separate confirmed `field-exemptions` operation. Deploy workflows never mutate the serving schema.

`web/admin` has a separate TypeScript query contract at `web/admin/lib/__tests__/firestore-query-contract.test.ts`, run by `web-checks.yml` for changes under `web/admin/**` and `firestore.indexes.json`. `web/personas-open-source` queries Firestore client-side and is outside the Python guard; its only composite shapes (`messages`: `pluginId ASC, timestamp ASC` and `botName ASC, timestamp ASC`) are declared in the registry and READY in prod (verified 2026-10-01); its Firebase project is build-time configurable.

The real-Firestore oracle is `backend/scripts/firestore_index_oracle.py`, exposed as `index-oracle` in `.github/workflows/jit_qa_manual_operator.yml`. Run it when validating a query/index change against Firestore's actual planning response or investigating a suspected index gap. It is an oracle and does not provision indexes.

## Respond to a missing-index alert

The backend provisions a missing-index alert through `.github/scripts/ensure_firestore_missing_index_alert.py`. Follow `backend/docs/runbooks/firestore-missing-index.md`: confirm the actual query and platform suggestion, declare the composite or collection-group field requirement in the registry, regenerate the manifest, and verify the request after readiness. Never copy a suggested index directly into a project.
